summary: Configured /srv/drop on node1 as a shared writable directory (owned root:dropusers, mode 1777 with sticky bit) so all members of the dropusers group can create files but only file owners (or root) can delete/rename others' files. Verified with two test users before and after a full node restart; boot ID changed confirming a genuine reboot, and sticky-bit enforcement plus directory ownership/permissions persisted correctly after recovery.
actions_performed: Created dropusers group and /srv/drop directory owned root:dropusers with mode 1777 (world-writable + sticky bit)
Created two test users (dropuser1, dropuser2) in dropusers group to validate cross-user behavior
Verified dropuser2 could NOT delete a file created by dropuser1 in /srv/drop (Operation not permitted)
Verified each user CAN create and delete their own files in /srv/drop
Captured baseline boot_id and /srv/drop state on node1
Issued non-interactive reboot (shutdown -r now) on node1, acknowledgement returned before disconnect
Polled node1 until exec access returned; confirmed boot_id changed, proving a real restart
Re-verified /srv/drop ownership/permissions and sticky-bit protection post-restart with a fresh cross-user delete test

evidence.requirement: /srv/drop exists as a shared writable directory with correct ownership/permissions (1777, root:dropusers)
evidence.summary: stat shows drwxrwxrwt root dropusers 1777 /srv/drop immediately after creation

evidence.requirement: Users cannot remove files owned by other users (sticky bit enforcement)
evidence.summary: dropuser2's attempt to rm dropuser1's file failed with 'Operation not permitted'; owners could delete their own files successfully
Captured boot_id 15443601-... and confirmed /srv/drop state (1777, root:dropusers) before restart

evidence.requirement: Node1 restart acknowledgement returned before disconnect
evidence.summary: shutdown -r now issued and acknowledged; subsequent exec call failed with connection reset, confirming the node went down

evidence.requirement: Node1 boot identity changed after restart
evidence.summary: boot_id changed from 15443601-befc-4fc4-aa76-b417968ad3f9 to 14772eed-45f2-499f-a6ff-e58856a56216, proving an actual reboot occurred

evidence.requirement: Post-restart recovery of /srv/drop and sticky-bit behavior
evidence.summary: After restart, /srv/drop retained 1777 root:dropusers; repeated cross-user delete test again correctly denied dropuser2 from removing dropuser1's file, and owner cleanup succeeded
